key_insight: Pre-trained simple neural networks (MLPs), whether trained on low-resolution LAMOST spectra or on learned spectral embeddings, can be fine-tuned to deliver accurate stellar-parameter estimates on DESI medium-resolution spectra—achieving reliable cross-survey generalization with limited labeled data.
problem_solved: Addresses the domain shift and resolution mismatch when transferring spectral-parameter models from low-resolution surveys (LAMOST) to moderate-resolution surveys (DESI), reducing the need for large labeled datasets in the target survey.
method: Pre-train lightweight MLPs on LAMOST low-resolution spectra or on embeddings derived from those spectra.
Fine-tune the pre-trained MLPs on a small labeled subset of DESI medium-resolution spectra (case study: LAMOST → DESI).
Evaluate transfer performance vs. training-from-scratch and compare embedding-based vs. raw-spectra pre-training for robustness to resolution gaps.
impact: Shows that simple architectures plus transfer learning can bridge instrument and resolution differences, enabling fast, label-efficient deployment of spectral-parameter models across surveys—useful for practitioners who need scalable, maintainable pipelines without complex architectures.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Pre-train on LAMOST (raw spectra or embeddings) → Fine-tune on small DESI labeled set → Predict stellar parameters.
Bar/box-chart comparing parameter errors (Teff, log g, [Fe/H]) for: from-scratch, pre-trained-on-raw, pre-trained-on-embeddings.
Embedding projection (UMAP/t-SNE) colored by survey and stellar labels showing alignment before and after fine-tuning.
Learning-curve plot: validation error vs. number of DESI labels to illustrate sample-efficiency gains from transfer.
paper_title: Generalization from Low- to Moderate-Resolution Spectra with Neural Networks for Stellar Parameter Estimation: A Case Study with DESI
paper_authors: Xiaosheng Zhao, Yuan-Sen Ting, Rosemary F. G. Wyse, Alexander S. Szalay, Yang Huang
